summary: Iteration 9 (Notification Center + Webhook Docs) tested end-to-end. Backend: all 6 pytest cases pass — notifications CRUD (list, unread-count, per-workspace scoping), traffic_blocked producer via /api/r/{alias} with bot UA + datacenter IP (throttling verified: 2nd bot click within the hour does NOT create a duplicate), webhook_failed producer via httpbin 500 after 3 retries (~7s), member_joined producer via invite→register→accept. Mark-read / read-all / dismiss all confirmed working and correctly decrement unread_count. Frontend: NotificationBell renders in dashboard header, popover opens on click, empty state (notif-empty) renders correctly ('You're all caught up.'), badge disappears after mark-all-read. Webhook docs page (/app/developers): webhook-docs-card present, all 4 events (click.recorded / click.blocked / click.challenged / ping) and 3 headers (X-MidGate-Event / Delivery / Signature) rendered; all 3 tabs (payload/node/php) switch correctly and expose copy buttons.
critical_code_review_comments: notifications.py list_notifications() caps items at 50 — fine for MVP but no pagination cursor for older items; consider adding skip/limit params before scaling.

notify_throttled dedupe key uses meta.dedupe with a created_at range scan — no index on (workspace_id, type, meta.dedupe, created_at); may become slow >_MAX_KEEP (200). Constant _MAX_KEEP is defined but never enforced (no trimming logic).
NotificationBell polls unread-count every 30s per mounted instance — acceptable, but consider pausing polling when tab is hidden (document.visibilityState) to save requests.
Delete notification returns {ok: true} even if id does not exist (delete_one silently no-ops) — should return 404 for consistency with other endpoints (webhooks/team).
seed_data_creation: Each test creates its own resources (link, webhook, invited user) and cleans up (delete link, delete webhook, dismiss notification, remove member). No residual test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest for iter9 is at /app/backend/tests/test_iter9_notifications.py — reuse for regression. Notes: link creation POST /api/links REQUIRES 'name' (422 otherwise). Login response returns {user, workspace:{id,...}}; use workspace.id as X-Workspace-Id header. Notifications feed is shared per workspace (single read flag) — do not assume per-user unread. Throttling windows: traffic_blocked=3600s, webhook_failed=1800s (per webhook_id).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in iter9.
